questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of interrupt handling, latency, and concurrency without requiring full kernel onboarding. Two sources with differing workloads highlight top-half vs bottom-half design choices and fairness.

## Key Concepts
- Top-half vs bottom-half interrupt handling
- Per-CPU workqueues and lock-free communication
- Scheduler wakeups and fairness across cores

## Code Example
```c
// pseudo
interrupt timer_isr() { tick++; if (needs_work()) enqueue(BOTTOM, TIMER_EVENT); }
interrupt io_isr() { enqueue(BOTTOM, IO_EVENT); }
void bottom_worker() { while (pop(EVENT)) handle(EVENT); }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test latency under bursty IO?
- How would you extend to multiple hardware IRQs with prioritization?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of per-core data locality, lock-free synchronization, and work-stealing basics in a beginner-friendly OS context. 

## Key Concepts
- Per-core queues and locality
- Work-stealing and fairness
- Lock-free CAS and memory barriers
- False sharing considerations

## Code Example
```c
// Minimal sketch (pseudo-code)
typedef struct { volatile int head, tail; Task* buf[CAP]; } Deque;
void push(Deque* d, Task* t){ int i = atomic_fetch_add(&d->tail, 1); d->buf[i % CAP] = t; }
Task* pop(Deque* d){ int t = --d->tail; if (t >= d->head) return d->buf[t % CAP]; return NULL; }
Task* steal(Deque* nd){ // neighbor's deque; atomically take half
  int h = nd->head; int t = nd->tail; if (h >= t) return NULL; Task* s = nd->buf[h % CAP]; nd->head = h+1; return s; }
```

- How would you test starvation? 
- How would you extend to dynamic capacity and NUMA-awareness?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question probes practical NUMA-aware memory management, concurrency, and IO paths under contention. It requires precise state machines and race-free synchronization.

## Key Concepts

- NUMA-aware allocation
- per-page state machine NONE/PENDING/VALID
- CAS-based serialization to avoid duplicate fetch
- cross-node IO queues and read-ahead

## Code Example

```c
// Minimal sketch
typedef enum { NONE, PENDING, VALID } page_state_t;
struct page { atomic_int state; void *frame; int io_inflight; };
void handle_fault(struct page *p) { if (cas(&p->state, NONE, PENDING)) { enqueue_io(p); } else { wait_on_page(p); } }
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you test contention and ensure liveness?
- How to extend for write-back coherency and cache eviction?
